kevin-cust: Hey all — our Private deployment (VPC) started failing for some requests since ~08:30 UTC. Generation calls intermittently return 502 or 401 shortly after model pull. No changes on our side. Can you confirm what outbound hosts/ports we must allow? Seeing TLS handshake errors in worker logs.

maria-support: sorry you're hitting this, @kevin-cust. Can you paste the small error snippet and a quick repro? Also can you run a couple quick checks from one of the worker nodes and post output: 

1) nslookup / dig for model registry + auth
2) curl -v against auth and telemetry endpoints
3) openssl s_client to check TLS/SNI

Example commands: 
```
nslookup models.redwood.ai
curl -v https://auth.redwood.ai/oauth/token
openssl s_client -connect telemetry.redwood.ai:443 -servername telemetry.redwood.ai
```

kevin-cust: paste of the error logs (sanitized):
```
2026-03-16T08:33:12Z worker-3 ERROR token_refresh failed: TLS handshake error: remote error: tls: bad certificate
2026-03-16T08:33:12Z worker-3 WARN model pull failed: 502 Bad Gateway from gateway
```
I ran the three checks — attaching outputs:

1) nslookup models.redwood.ai -> CNAME -> models.s3-us-west-2.amazonaws.com
2) curl -v https://auth.redwood.ai/oauth/token -> "* TLS handshake error: alert handshake failure"
3) openssl s_client shows the connection drops during cert verify (no cert returned)

maria-support: thanks — that points at TLS interception or blocked OCSP/CRL/OCSP stapling endpoints. Two things commonly break private deployments:
- MITM TLS inspection that rewrites SNI or replaces certs (breaks token fetch and model registry cert validation)
- Egress allowlist missing CRL/OCSP or S3 endpoints for model artifacts

jon-infra: adding the minimal allowlist we recommend for Private deployments (outbound TCP):
- auth.redwood.ai:443
- api.redwood.ai:443
- telemetry.redwood.ai:443
- models.redwood.ai (CNAME -> S3) -> allow *.s3.amazonaws.com and region endpoints (e.g., s3.us-west-2.amazonaws.com):443
- packages.redwood.ai (if you use our hosted packages):443
- registry-1.docker.io:443, ghcr.io:443, gcr.io:443 (image pulls)
- registry.npmjs.org:443, registry.yarnpkg.com:443, registry.npmjs.org:443
- pypi.org:443, files.pythonhosted.org:443, crl and ocsp endpoints below

Also allow these certificate/CRL/OCSP endpoints (TLS cert validation and stapling):
- ocsp.int-x3.letsencrypt.org:80/443 (Let's Encrypt OCSP)
- ocsp.digicert.com:80/443
- crl3.digicert.com:80/443
- crl.identrust.com:80/443

Ports: primarily TCP 443 (HTTPS). Some OCSP/CRL endpoints use port 80. Ensure outbound 80/443 allowed to above hosts.

amy-sre: Important note: if your perimeter performs TLS interception (corporate proxy that does MITM), you must either: 
- add exceptions to bypass MITM for the Redwood hosts above (TLS passthrough), OR
- install the intercepting CA into the worker's OS/truststore AND ensure it is present for all runtime containers.
If TLS inspection rewrites SNI or strips OCSP stapling, token refresh and certificate validation will fail — leads to the logs you pasted.

maria-support: repro steps for us to validate once you update allowlist / bypass MITM:
1) from a worker node before change: `curl -v https://auth.redwood.ai/oauth/token` (should show TLS handshake error)
2) after change: rerun same curl; success will return JSON token response (200)
3) verify model object fetch: `curl -I https://models.redwood.ai/<model-path>` — expect 200 + correct Content-Type and S3 redirect if behind S3
4) check ocsp/CRL reachability: `curl -v https://ocsp.int-x3.letsencrypt.org` (should connect; 200 or HTTP/1.1 responses can vary)

Example quick debug commands we asked for above (copy/paste):
```
# DNS + trace
dig +short models.redwood.ai\curl -v https://auth.redwood.ai/oauth/token 2>&1 | sed -n '1,120p'
openssl s_client -connect auth.redwood.ai:443 -servername auth.redwood.ai -status
```

kevin-cust: ran the openssl with -status and we see "no response data available" and connection drops. We don't have a TLS MITM bypass rule enabled currently. We'll ask infra to open exceptions for the listed hosts and add OCSP/CRL.

jon-infra: quick checklist for infra teams:
- Allow outbound TCP 443 to the hosts list (wildcards where necessary for S3 and package registries)
- Allow outbound TCP 80/443 to OCSP/CRL endpoints (Let's Encrypt, DigiCert, IdenTrust)
- Add TLS passthrough bypass on the corporate TLS proxy for *.redwood.ai, *.s3.amazonaws.com, registry-1.docker.io, ghcr.io, gcr.io
- If bypass can't be done, distribute proxy CA to the worker/trusted store and restart services

ops-bot: Ticket #SUP-2026-412 created and escalated to Infra oncall — assigned to @jon-infra :rotating_light:

maria-support: looping in @amy-sre for SRE/TLS guidance — amy, any additional checks?

amy-sre: please also capture a packet capture of the TLS handshake if the above changes don't resolve it. Look for CLIENT_HELLO SNI field present and SERVER_HELLO/cert messages. If a proxy responds with its own cert, that's the MITM.

kevin-cust: thanks all, infra team will implement allowlist + passthrough exceptions and confirm back here once tested. Appreciate the checklist 🙏

maria-support: ping us after you test and we'll validate from our side. Closing once you confirm OK.
